claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is single-phase fcc.
The initial FeCoNi alloy is a high-entropy alloy.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field no greater than 100 Oe.
Adding a secondary magnetic phase with higher anisotropy will increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi beyond 100 Oe.
The introduced secondary phase will enhance the composite's overall magnetic anisotropy.
Increased magnetic anisotropy produces higher energy barriers for magnetic domain-wall movement.
Higher energy barriers to domain-wall movement increase coercivity.
The resulting composite will have a coercive field exceeding 100 Oe relative to the original single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The exact nature and composition of the secondary phase may affect the outcome.
The interactions between the primary and secondary phases are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that introducing an appropriate secondary phase will exceed 100 Oe, but the falsification rule rejects the entire hypothesis if any member of a varying-phase-fraction series fails to exceed 100 Oe. This is stronger than the stated prediction and would treat an ineffective loading, including potentially negligible secondary-phase content, as decisive falsification.
